title: CIRPASS-2 EUDPP Core Ontology
usedFor: EU DPP pilot requirements feeding CEN/CENELEC JTC 24. The closest community profile to the standards track we are actually measured against.
licence: Apache-2.0 (code) / CC BY 4.0 (document) dual grant, with an explicit dispute-resolution fallback clause naming CC BY 4.0. Confirmed 2026-08-11 from the ontology file's own `dcterms:license` header — this statement is not on any of CIRPASS-2's public web pages (`cirpass2.eu/project-results/` states no licence at all), only inside the file itself, exactly the kind of thing a survey would miss.
source: https://w3id.org/eudpp — fetched directly, all 8 imported modules (ACTOR, CON, EVENT, IDENT, MAT, P_DPP, SOC, COMP) resolved and read.
finding: The IRI resolves — confirmed live, HTTP 303 redirect to a Semantic Treehouse-family backend serving Turtle (content-negotiable via `?format=ttl`) — settling the 'does it even resolve' half of the prior open question. The root document is a pure import index declaring `owl:versionInfo "2.0.5"`; module versions are **not in lockstep** with it (ACTOR declares `2.0.0` separately) — citing 'v2.0.5' as if every module carries that number would be wrong. Per-module term counts landed close to the higher of the two previously-reported figures (233 vs 338) — roughly 338 across two independent fetch-and-count passes — but individual module sub-counts wobbled by single digits between passes even when reading the primary source directly, which is the same class of error that produced the original 233-vs-338 dispute in the first place. The `COMP` module already models `EUDeclarationOfConformity`/`ConformityCertificate`/`HarmonisedStandard` in ESPR-native shape, more directly than SEMIC's CCCEV does; `EVENT` is notably rich (94 terms) for anything EPCIS-shaped.
nextStep: Run an actual RDF parser (rdflib / Apache Jena `riot` / ROBOT) over the 8 downloaded `.ttl` files for an authoritative term count — not another read-and-eyeball pass, which is the method that produced the wobble twice now. Gap-source only for now, not a map target: it's a EU-funded pilot ontology, not a ratified standard, its own versioning is internally inconsistent, and JTC 24 (the actual standards track) may diverge from it. Revisit mapping once EN 18223 is read and can be checked against the `COMP` module's boundaries for alignment.
